stories.title: Thai teen’s viral guitar solos fuel hopes for tourism boost
stories.summary: Thai teen guitarist Nene Royal gained viral fame on America’s Got Talent with over 200 million views, raising hopes of boosting Thailand's international tourism. Thai officials, including the Prime Minister, support Nene and consider featuring her in the "Amazing Thailand" tourism campaign. Nene's popularity has increased demand for guitars and music lessons in Thailand, inspiring young people to learn music and pursue global artistic dreams. Thailand is rallying behind a 16-year-old guitarist whose viral run on America’s Got Talent (AGT) is raising hopes she can draw fresh international attention and, eventually, more tourists to the country. Rattikarn Amloy, who performs as Nene Royal, shot to fame with a swaggering rendition of The Cranberries’ Zombie, singing and ripping through guitar solos that quickly spread across social media. Her appearances have since amassed more than 200 million views across AGT’s official online platforms, more than any other act in 2026. Thai officials have welcomed Nene’s rise and hope her growing international profile can bolster tourism promotion. Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul instructed the tourism authorities to explore ways to support Nene after seeing her perform and later hosted her at Government House, where she accompanied him as he sang a Thai rock song. The government has also discussed featuring her in campaigns for the “Amazing Thailand” brand. Entertainment and popular culture have helped keep Thailand visible overseas. Most recently, HBO’s The White Lotus put the country’s luxury resorts and tropical scenery before a vast international audience and fuelled interest in visiting its filming locations. The potential lift comes at a crucial time for one of Thailand’s biggest economic engines.

stories.title: China opposes unilateral US sanctions — embassy in Washington
stories.summary: Chinese Embassy Spokesman Liu Chang stressed that Beijing will protect Chinese businesses’ legitimate and lawful rights and interests
article_sentences: WASHINGTON, August 25.
Beijing opposes illegal unilateral US sanctions and will firmly protect the rights and interests of Chinese companies, Chinese Embassy Spokesman Liu Chang told TASS on Monday.
"We stand firmly against illicit unilateral sanctions that have no basis in international law or the authorization of the UN Security Council.

We will firmly protect Chinese businesses’ legitimate and lawful rights and interests," Liu Chang said in response to the inclusion of Chinese individuals and entities on the US sanctions list targeting Iran.
On Monday, the US administration added 48 entities, 24 individuals and six oil tankers to its Iran sanctions list.

The blacklist included individuals and companies from Azerbaijan, Greece, India, Iran, China, Malaysia, the Marshall Islands, the United Arab Emirates, Singapore, Turkey, Ukraine, France and Switzerland.

stories.title: Ukraine needs transitional administration, not just elections — ex-PM
stories.summary: Nikolay Azarov noted that if elections were held under Ukraine's current political conditions, manipulation and fraud would allow representatives of the existing regime to come to power again
article_sentences: MOSCOW, August 25.

Holding elections alone will not bring about a change of regime in Ukraine, which instead requires serious talks with the United States resulting in the creation of a transitional administration before elections can be organized, former Ukrainian Prime Minister Nikolay Azarov told TASS.
He said that if elections were held under Ukraine's current political conditions, manipulation and fraud would allow representatives of the existing regime to come to power again.
"What difference will elections make now, in these circumstances?
They will elect whoever needs to be elected - that is completely obvious.
Will the current regime remain in place?
Of course it will," Azarov said.

"To avoid such a scenario [in which the Kiev regime remains in place], very serious talks with the Americans are needed, along with arguments that could persuade the current US administration to make certain concrete compromises.
What would those concrete compromises be?
First and foremost, a transitional administration and elections overseen by certain bodies that would prevent Nazis from coming to power again," he concluded.

stories.title: Rescuers find cabins carrying tourists swept away from thermal springs on Sakhalin
stories.summary: Rescuers landed at the thermal springs and have now set off on foot toward the location where the containers were found
article_sentences: YUZHNO-SAKHALINSK, August 25.

Rescuers conducting an aerial survey on Sakhalin found container cabins carrying tourists that had been swept away by a river from the Lesogorsk thermal springs, the regional directorate of the Russian Emergencies Ministry told TASS.
"Rescuers have just located the containers.
A helicopter has joined the search.
As there are no roads in the emergency area, the territory had previously been searched on foot.
The helicopter crew spotted the cabins but cannot land near them.
Rescuers landed at the thermal springs and have now set off on foot toward the location where the containers were found," the ministry said.
It added that nine rescuers are aboard the helicopter, while a ground team is also working at the site.
